doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
title: Walking club costumes and clarinet reeds
summary: Callers ask about the walking club costumes (pilgrims) and Pete's reed strength and brand; Ramsey tells a Paul Desmond joke.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Thank you for calling. Okay. Bye-bye. Hope you can get together. 522-3791. Hello. Go ahead.
Turn your radio off and go ahead.
The radio is off. I would like to ask Pete one thing about, curious about what kind of costumes the boys are going to be wearing this year for the walking club.
We will be pilgrims this year. Pardon? We will be pilgrims this year. Pilgrims? You mean like Puritans? Right. Puritans. Pilgrims.
Another question. Pete, what... What number of reads do you use on your clarinet by any chance?
Two and a half. It's Bernard.
Right. It's three special or two and a half, which is equivalent to about a two and a half, really.

Two and a half to three. Two and a half to three. Right. They don't come in... Bernard doesn't come in a half, but it's either two or three. So I'll get a box of threes and I can pick out about a two and a half out of it.

Thank you. Thank you. Shall we get the other question out of the way? What size mouthpiece do you use? The leg. The leg, you know. I told these guys during the break that Paul Desmond, the great alto saxophone player with the Brubeck Group for so many years, is writing a book about his experiences with the band. And the title of the book is going to be a question that he was incessantly asked on airplanes by stewardesses. And that was, how many of you are there in the quartet? In the quartet. Yeah. Here's another call. Hello. Go ahead, please.
